# AGENTS.md — working on this repository

This repo is a catalog of OpenCode skills. Read `CATALOG.md` first; it lists every
skill, agent, and command with its path.

## Source of truth

| Thing | Source | Generated |
|-------|--------|-----------|
| Skills | `skills/<kebab-name>/` | `.opencode/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` |
| Agents | `agents/*.md` (flat, final names) | `.opencode/agents/*.md` |
| Commands | `commands/**/*.md` | `.opencode/commands/**/*.md` |
| Catalog | the tree above | `CATALOG.md` |

Never edit `.opencode/` or `CATALOG.md` by hand. After moving or renaming anything:

```bash
python3 scripts/build-agents.py
python3 scripts/catalog.py
```

Both have `--check` and fail on drift.

## Contracts

- An agent's frontmatter `name` must equal its file stem. Allowed keys:
  `name`, `mode`, `description`, `permission`; mode is `primary` or `subagent`;
  permissions are `read`, `edit`, `bash`, `task` with `allow|deny|ask`.
- Skill scripts resolve the repo root from `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]`
  (script → skill → skills → repo). Never resolve from `$PWD`.
- Installed skills must stay self-contained: `SKILL.md`, `scripts/`, `templates/`,
  `workflows/`, `profiles/`.
- Local registry is the default. The MCP server in `registry-server/` is optional and
  must fail closed: no `REGISTRY_API_KEY` → `503`, wrong key → `401`.

## Checks before a change is done

```bash
npm test
python3 scripts/catalog.py --check
python3 scripts/build-agents.py --check
node registry-server/test/run.mjs
```

The design gate is the reason this repo exists: an untouched design-system template,
uniform entrance motion, or an empty visual audit must fail, not pass. Do not weaken
`detect-slop.py` to make a site pass; fix the design.

# init-frontend — Master Skill

## Trigger

Use `@init-frontend` when the task is to initialize a new frontend project with a design system — not just scaffolding. Triggers: "init frontend", "frontend init", "scaffold frontend", "new frontend project", "design system init", "frontend setup".

**Golden Rule: Questions First, Code Second.** No code is written until ALL design questions are answered.

## Commands (`ufmw/`)

| Command | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `ufmw init-frontend <project-name> [type]` | Scaffold new project (structure, tokens, component library, responsive base, a11y, perf budget, CI) |
| `ufmw init-frontend tokens` | Initialize design-token tier + Style Dictionary build |
| `ufmw init-frontend component <name>` | Add component with full state matrix, stories, a11y test |
| `ufmw init-frontend template <category>` | Download template by category, re-apply init-frontend principles |
| `ufmw init-frontend audit` | Run quality gates: token audit, static a11y, performance budget, responsive check |

Template categories: landing, portfolio, blog, ecommerce, dashboard, admin, saas, docs, restaurant, realestate, event, nonprofit, resume, plus examples/ (12 example sites).

## Profiles

| Profile | Constraints |
|---------|-------------|
| basic | Tokens, component library, responsive base, a11y, perf budget, CI |
| advanced | All basic + state matrix per component, stories, CI-enforced perf budget, words-first design direction, coverage gates |

## Mandatory Question-First Flow (before any code)

The agent asks ALL of these via chat. No code is written until every question is answered:

1. **Project name** (required)
2. **Template type** (default: landing) — landing, portfolio, blog, ecommerce, dashboard, admin, saas, docs, restaurant, realestate, event, nonprofit, resume, or custom
3. **Profile** (default: basic) — basic or advanced
4. **Background** (choose one or more): solid color, gradient, background image, background video, dark theme, light theme, system preference, brand primary color, brand accent color, none
5. **Animation** (choose one or more): fade-in on load, slide-up on scroll, parallax scrolling, hover effects, page transitions, loading spinner/skeleton, staggered list reveals, none
6. **Reference websites** (optional): URLs you like — researched before design decisions
7. **Interactivity** (choose one or more): hover state changes, click/tap behaviors, form validation, modal dialogs, carousel/slider, mobile hamburger menu, sticky navigation, scroll-to-top button, none
8. **Content sections** (choose one or more): hero, about, services, portfolio/work, testimonials, contact, pricing, FAQ, blog/news, none/custom
9. **Typography**: 14 font pairings or custom or system fonts only
10. **Color palette**: 13 curated palettes or custom colors or none/defaults

Each question has multiple choices + "none" / "custom" option. Nothing is assumed.

## Research Phase (before design decisions)

Reference URLs provided are researched via `ask-matt` subagent before design decisions:
- Extracts color schemes, typography, layout patterns, interaction styles
- Findings feed into design token choices
- You approve or adjust before scaffold

## Anti-AI-Slop Rules

1. No Inter by default — choose a typeface appropriate to the project type.
2. No purple/blue gradients.
3. No hero+3-cards boilerplate.
4. No glassmorphism.
5. No sub-24px touch targets.
6. No removed focus outlines.
7. Words first — content and hierarchy before decoration.
8. Constraints before options — encode limits, don't offer endless choice.

## Accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA)

- Semantic HTML throughout.
- `focus-visible` rings on all interactive elements.
- Real labels for every input (never placeholder-only).
- ≥4.5:1 text contrast / ≥3:1 UI contrast.
- Full keyboard navigation.
- Reduced-motion support.
- Verified with static a11y gate (scripts/a11y.cjs).

## Performance Budgets (P75, mobile + desktop)

- LCP ≤ 2.5s
- INP ≤ 200ms
- CLS ≤ 0.1
- Input budget total ≤ 1.5MB
- JS ≤ 300KB
- CSS ≤ 100KB
- LCP image ≤ 200KB

## Workflow

1. Read `.ufme/AGENT_STATE.md`, `.ufme/TASKS.md`, `.ufme/ENVIRONMENT.md`.
2. Ask ALL design questions via chat (background, animation, references, interactivity, content, typography, color).
3. Research reference URLs (if provided) via `ask-matt`.
4. Run `skills/universal-frontend-master/scripts/init-project.py` to record answers in `.ufme/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` and `.ufme/design-choices.json`.
5. Run `scripts/init-frontend.sh <project-name> [type]` (this skill) to scaffold (only after questions answered).
6. Initialize design tokens (`ufmw init-frontend tokens`).
7. Configure CI with perf budget and a11y gates.
8. Run `ufmw init-frontend audit` to verify WCAG 2.2 AA + performance budgets.
9. Update `.ufme/AGENT_STATE.md` and `.ufme/TASKS.md` after each step.

## Prohibited

- Do not run `sudo`, `pacman`, `systemctl`, `doas`, `pkexec`, or `su`.
- Do not install system packages.
- No Playwright, no containers.
- No removed focus outlines, no sub-24px targets, no Inter by default.
- Do not silently bypass missing dependencies — record in `.ufme/ENVIRONMENT.md`, prompt the user, mark BLOCKED.
- Do NOT scaffold before design questions are answered.

## Delegation

- No sub-agents by default (single-agent architecture). For complex multi-template projects, delegate to `@ufmw-frontend-design` for reference-driven design work.

# ufmw-frontend-design

## Trigger

Use @ufmw-frontend-design to build, improve, redesign, integrate, or audit a website frontend from a brief, repository, API documentation, screenshots, or one or more live design references. Users may select individual elements from reference sites and specify where and how to adapt them.

## Core Rules

1. Never invent backend endpoints, fields, or roles. Implement only capabilities confirmed by the project's API and authentication contracts.
2. Preserve the existing stack. Record a justified decision before changing frameworks, build tools, or architecture.
3. Never run sudo, pacman, systemctl, doas, pkexec, or su. Never install system packages. Do not use Playwright or containers for this skill.
4. Preserve browser sandboxing. Explicit CI flags may differ when configured by the workflow.
5. Verify asset and library licenses before adding dependencies. Record material decisions and new dependencies.
6. Base audits on fresh evidence. Missing prerequisites must remain BLOCKED or SKIPPED, never silently pass.
7. Do not treat generated reference notes as completed application implementation. Implement in the target project's actual framework and component architecture.

## Agent Collaboration

The primary agent decides how to collaborate based on the task. It may work directly, use the orchestrator, invoke any useful specialist, use available MCP servers, research, tools, and parallel execution. Do not impose a fixed agent roster, mandatory sequence, delegation count, concurrency cap, or allowlist.

Profiles in profiles/ are advisory guidance for research depth, verification depth, browser coverage, and resource intensity. They never restrict collaboration, agent selection, tools, MCP servers, delegation, or parallelism. Safety requirements remain in force.

Available specialists include ufmw-orchestrator, ufmw-designer, ufmw-builder, ufme-backend-analyst, and ufmw-auditor. They are options, not required roles.

## Shared Script Dependency

This skill depends on universal-frontend-master for its shared scripts, browser runner, quality gates, templates, and evidence helpers. The installer must resolve this dependency when this skill is selected. In a checkout, helpers live in skills/universal-frontend-master/scripts/; after global installation they live in the corresponding OpenCode skill directory.

## Reference-Driven Design

1. Collect reference URLs supplied by the user. Do not require a reference for unrelated frontend work.
2. Inspect each URL with reference-inspect.js. Evidence is retained per URL and screenshots are stored separately.
3. Run reference-analyze.py to create or update REFERENCES.md and ELEMENT_MAP.md. Re-analysis must preserve existing element selections and mappings.
4. Let the user select only elements they want. Record the intended destination and aspects (visual appearance, behavior, animation, layout, or a combination). Untouched placeholders are not selected mappings.
5. Run reference-match.py. A mapping is matched only when it resolves to real source evidence and contains a destination and intended aspects.
6. Run reference-adapt.py to prepare an implementation brief from measured source styles. The script does not edit application source code; implement the adaptation in the target framework, component conventions, design tokens, semantics, and responsive behavior.
7. Run reference-verify.js with the target URL after implementation. It inspects both pages and compares selected selectors, using each element's own reference URL. Style comparison does not prove behavior or animation; those require interaction-specific checks and must be reported separately.

## Shared Helpers

The scripts are provided by universal-frontend-master:

| Script | Purpose |
|---|---|
| reference-inspect.js | Inspect a live reference and capture DOM, computed styles, and unique element selectors/screenshots |
| reference-analyze.py | Build or update the reference catalog, stable element IDs, and mapping file |
| reference-match.py | Validate selected elements and create a match plan across references |
| reference-adapt.py | Produce a measured-style implementation brief |
| reference-verify.js | Compare selected reference and target elements |
| element-catalog.py | Maintain reusable reference-element records |
| detect-stack.sh | Detect the existing frontend stack and project scripts |
| browser-test.sh | Run native Selenium browser checks |
| audit-a11y.js | Run axe-core accessibility checks |
| audit-perf.sh | Run Lighthouse performance checks |
| visual-diff.js | Compare browser screenshots |
| quality-check.py | Combine test and audit evidence into a quality report |
| self-improve.py | Review skill source and installed copies |

## OpenCode Commands

These are OpenCode slash commands, not a standalone uFMW shell executable:

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| /ufmw/reference-add | Add a reference URL |
| /ufmw/reference-analyze | Inspect/analyze reference URLs and generate the element map |
| /ufmw/reference-inspect | Inspect a selected element |
| /ufmw/reference-list | List known references |
| /ufmw/reference-match | Validate selected mappings |
| /ufmw/reference-adapt | Prepare implementation briefs |
| /ufmw/reference-verify | Verify implemented reference elements |
| /profile/lite, /profile/standard, /profile/advanced, /profile/autonomous | Select advisory execution depth |

## Quality and Delivery

- Implement selected elements rather than stopping at analysis or generated notes.
- Preserve accessible semantics, keyboard behavior, responsive layouts, reduced-motion preferences, and existing project contracts.
- Run relevant project tests, browser checks, accessibility/performance/visual audits, and security checks.
- Fix findings and repeat affected checks.
- Record what was actually run, failures, blocked checks, and remaining limitations.

## Compatibility

This skill uses the shared universal-frontend-master helpers and is compatible with ufmw-seo-protocol. Both use the project .ufme memory directory. The installer resolves declared skill dependencies automatically.

Use `@ufmw-seo-protocol` when the task is to audit, optimize, or monitor a website for search engine optimization — technical SEO, on-page SEO, content optimization, structured data, internal linking, crawlability, indexing diagnostics, rendering analysis, redirects, sitemap validation, robots.txt analysis, keyword research, search-intent analysis, content-gap detection, or performance optimization for SEO.

## Hard Rules

1. Never fabricate search metrics. Report only measured data from crawl, Lighthouse, axe-core, or Google Search Console (when credentials are configured). Mock data must be clearly labeled as fixtures.
2. Preserve the existing website architecture. Inspect each target website before modifying it; use its existing framework, routing, components, and metadata implementation.
3. Apply only safe, non-destructive SEO fixes by default (meta tags, alt text, canonical tags, structured data, sitemap, robots.txt). Framework migrations or wholesale rewrites require explicit user approval.
4. Never run `sudo`, `pacman`, `systemctl`, `doas`, `pkexec`, or `su`; never install system packages; no Playwright, no containers; browser sandbox preserved.
5. Evidence-first SEO: read `.ufme/evidence/seo-results.json`, `seo-crawl.json`, `seo-plan.json` BEFORE making changes; verify fixes by re-crawling.

## Agent Router

| `ufmw seo init` | Initialize SEO project memory |

```bash
ufmw seo run --profile autonomous --mode full --apply-safe
```

Executes the complete SEO workflow: discovery → crawl → analyze → plan → implement → verify → report → monitor.

# universal-frontend-master

## Trigger

Use `@universal-frontend-master` when the task is building or improving a responsive website frontend — starting from a project brief, an existing repo, API documentation, a screenshot, or a reference site — or extending, redesigning, integrating, or quality-checking (visual, accessibility, performance, security) an existing frontend. ## Hard rules

1. Never invent backend endpoints, fields, or roles. Implement only CONFIRMED capabilities from `.ufme/API_MAP.md`; anything else is INFERRED/NOT_FOUND and stays unimplemented.

3. **Profile** (default: basic) — basic or advanced

5. **Animation** (choose one or more): fade-in on load, slide-up on scroll, parallax scrolling, hover effects, page transitions, loading spinner/skeleton, staggered list reveals, none

- Real labels for every input (never placeholder-only).

- Full keyboard navigation.
- Reduced-motion support.

- CLS ≤ 0.1

- CSS ≤ 100KB

# universal-frontend-master — OpenCode Skill

## Primary entry point agent: `@universal-frontend-master`

Invoke this agent directly with `@universal-frontend-master` to start a frontend engineering session. It is the only user-facing primary agent; it resolves the active execution profile and delegates according to `allowedAgents` — to `ufme-orchestrator` for specialist coordination (advanced, autonomous) or directly to permitted specialists (lite, standard).

## Proper workflow (multi-agent pipeline)

Follow this workflow in order. Do not skip stages.

### Phase 1 — Intake (session start)

1. Read `.ufme/AGENT_STATE.md` and `.ufme/ENVIRONMENT.md`.
2. Detect whether the project is new, frontend-only, backend-only, or full-stack.
3. Detect the existing stack and preserve its architecture — do not force a framework change without technical justification recorded in `.ufme/DECISIONS.md`.
4. Set execution profile: `/profile/lite`, `/profile/standard`, `/profile/advanced`, or `/profile/autonomous` (default: `standard`).
5. Record the classification and stack in `.ufme/AGENT_STATE.md`.

### Phase 2 — Research

Delegate to `@ufme-designer` (research slice):
- Gather references, components, fonts, icons, images, videos.
- Verify licenses and commercial-use permissions.
- Record candidate libraries in `.ufme/LIBRARY_REGISTRY.md`.
- Maintain the shared user-level catalog at `~/.config/ufme/LIBRARY_REGISTRY.md` (available to every project).

### Phase 3 — Backend intelligence (mandatory)

Delegate to `@ufme-backend-analyst`:
- Parse OpenAPI/Swagger (JSON/YAML), Postman, GraphQL, AsyncAPI, and source hints for WebSocket/SSE/auth.
- Produce `.ufme/API_MAP.md`, `.ufme/BACKEND_CAPABILITIES.md`, `.ufme/AUTHENTICATION_MAP.md`, `.ufme/ERROR_HANDLING.md`.
- Mark capabilities as CONFIRMED / INFERRED / NOT_FOUND.

### Phase 4 — Product intelligence

Delegate to `@ufme-designer` (product slice):
- Create `.ufme/PRD.md`, `.ufme/SITEMAP.md`, `.ufme/USER_FLOWS.md`, `.ufme/FEATURES.md`.
- Map confirmed backend capabilities to frontend features; document gaps.

### Phase 5 — Design system

Delegate to `@ufme-designer`:
- Create `.ufme/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` (tokens, typography, spacing, color, components).
- Record any new asset (font, icon, image) in `.ufme/DECISIONS.md` before adding.

### Phase 6 — Architecture

Delegate to `@ufme-builder` (architecture slice):
- Define folder structure, routing, state management, data-fetching patterns, component boundaries, error boundaries, testing strategy.
- Preserve existing architecture unless justified.

### Phase 7 — Prototype (optional)

Run `scripts/generate-prototype.py` to build a static prototype from project artifacts.

### Phase 8 — Implementation

Delegate to `@ufme-builder` (implementation slice):
- Build pages, reusable components, navigation, forms, state, loading/error/empty states, responsive layouts, animations, PWA readiness where justified.
- Implement only backend capabilities confirmed by the backend analyst.
- Library installation is handled by the orchestrator via `scripts/search-libraries.py`.

### Phase 9 — Integration

Delegate to `@ufme-builder` (integration slice):
- Implement typed API clients, authentication flows, authorization-aware UI, validation, error handling, retries, network failure states.
- Only use endpoints confirmed by the backend analyst.

### Phase 10 — Browser execution

Run real Chromium/Firefox via Selenium WebDriver at four viewports (mobile, tablet, laptop, desktop), headless by default.
- `scripts/browser-test.sh` — run browser tests, write `browser-results.json`.
- `scripts/screenshot.sh` — capture viewport screenshots.
- No Playwright. No containers. No `--no-sandbox`.

### Phase 11 — Audits (fix and retest loop)

Run all four audits, fix critical/major findings, retest until pass or BLOCKED:

| Audit | Agent | Target |
|-------|-------|--------|
| Visual | `@ufme-auditor` | Selenium screenshots, alignment, spacing, typography, contrast, overflow |
| Accessibility | `@ufme-auditor` | WCAG 2.1 AA, semantic HTML, landmarks, headings, keyboard |
| Performance | `@ufme-auditor` | Core Web Vitals, bundle size, Lighthouse |
| Security | `@ufme-auditor` | XSS, CSRF, CORS, CSP, cookies, token storage, exposed secrets, dep audit |

### Phase 12 — Self-improvement

After each delivery run `scripts/self-improve.py` to audit:
- Source ↔ installed sync (agents, skill, scripts, docs)
- Script reference integrity (no stale `.sh` references)
- Phantom agent detection (no `@` mentions without agent files)
- Prohibited content sweep (hardcoded models, local paths, sudo/pacman/systemctl)
- Writes machine-readable JSON to `.ufme/evidence/self-improve-summary.json`

### Phase 13 — Delivery

Write quality report to `.ufme/evidence/quality-report.json`. Document limitations in `.ufme/AUDIT_REPORT.md`. Handover clean.

# UFME library-registry server

Optional MCP server that stores one shared library registry in Vercel Blob, with
a password-protected dashboard for API keys. The skill works without it; the
local Markdown registry stays the default.

## Endpoints

| Route | Method | Purpose |
|-------|--------|---------|
| `/mcp` | `POST` | JSON-RPC 2.0 MCP endpoint |
| `/health` | `GET` | liveness and configuration probe |
| `/` | `GET`/`POST` | API-key dashboard |

`/health` and `/` are rewritten in `vercel.json`. Both send
`x-robots-tag: noindex`.

## Auth

`/mcp` accepts `Authorization: Bearer <key>` where `<key>` is either:

- the bootstrap `REGISTRY_API_KEY` from the environment, or
- a key created in `/` (stored hashed).

| Case | Status |
|------|--------|
| No bootstrap key and no stored keys | `503` |
| Missing or wrong key | `401` |
| Valid request | `200` |

Keys created in the dashboard are shown once, stored as SHA-256 hashes, and
revoked by deleting the record.

## Health

```bash
curl -s https://your-app.vercel.app/health
# {"status":"ok","service":"ufme-library-registry","version":"1.0.0",
#  "auth":{"rootKey":true,"storedKeys":0}}

curl -s "https://your-app.vercel.app/health?deep=1"
# adds "entries": 52 (reads the registry)
```

| Case | Status | `status` |
|------|--------|----------|
| Bootstrap key or at least one stored key | `200` | `ok` |
| Neither configured | `503` | `unconfigured` |
| `?deep=1` and the registry cannot be read | `503` | `degraded` |
| On Vercel without Blob storage | `503` | `degraded` |

The response never contains key material. `storage` is `blob` when a Blob store
is configured and `local` otherwise.

## Admin dashboard

Set `REGISTRY_ADMIN_PASSWORD` (and optionally `REGISTRY_ADMIN_SECRET`) in the
Vercel project, then open `/`.

- Sign in with the password. The session is an HMAC-signed, `HttpOnly`,
  `SameSite=Strict` cookie valid for 12 hours.
- Create a key with a label; copy it from the one-time callout.
- Revoke any key; it stops working on the next `/mcp` request.
- POSTs require the double-submit CSRF token rendered into the form.
- Without `REGISTRY_ADMIN_PASSWORD` the dashboard returns `503` and no session
  can be created.

The dashboard is a single server-rendered page with an inline stylesheet and a
strict CSP; it loads no external assets.

## Bot protection

| Guard | Default | Env |
|-------|---------|-----|
| `/mcp` requests per minute per IP | 60 | `UFME_MCP_RATE_MAX` |
| Admin login attempts per minute per IP | 10 | `UFME_LOGIN_RATE_MAX` |
| JSON body size | 256 KiB | `UFME_MAX_BODY_BYTES` |

Exceeding a limit returns `429` with `retry-after`; an oversized body returns
`413`; a non-JSON content type on `/mcp` returns `415`.

The limiter is an in-memory fixed window per lambda instance, so it resets on
cold start and does not aggregate across instances. The free Hobby plan includes
3 WAF custom rules and 10 IP blocks at the edge — use one rule on `/mcp` and one
on `/` for distributed blocking. See `lib/limits.js`.

## Tools

| Tool | Arguments | Behaviour |
|------|-----------|-----------|
| `registry_list` | `query?`, `category?`, `status?`, `limit?` | filtered entries |
| `registry_get` | `name` | one entry |
| `registry_upsert` | entry fields | create or merge by `name` |
| `registry_remove` | `name` | delete |

Entry fields: `name`, `category`, `site` (https), `license`, `commercial`,
`install`, `reason`, `status` (`candidate|researched|approved|rejected`),
optional `npm`, `stars`.

Entries with `category: "theme"` may carry a `theme` object (`bg`, `surface`,
`text`, `muted`, `accent`, `accent_alt`, `display`, `body`, optional `mono`).
`theme-showcase.py` appends them to the local palette catalog.

## Storage

- With a Blob store: `ufme/library-registry.json` and `ufme/admin-keys.json`
  (`access: public`, `allowOverwrite: true`, `addRandomSuffix: false`).
  `BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN` works, and so does a store connected in the Vercel
  dashboard: the SDK then uses OIDC and `BLOB_STORE_ID`, with no long-lived token.
- Without one: `.data/library-registry.json` and `.data/admin-keys.json` next to
  this directory. Fine locally; ephemeral on Vercel.

On Vercel without a Blob store, `/health` reports `degraded` and `/` refuses
to create keys, because they would disappear when the instance recycles.

On first read, a missing registry falls back to `seed.json`; a missing key store
falls back to no keys.

## Deploy

This folder is a monorepo package: set the Vercel project's **Root Directory** to
`registry-server`, then push to `main` or run `vercel deploy` from here. The
runtime is pinned to Node 22 in `package.json` (`engines`); `nodejs26.x` still
emits the Vercel `DEP0169` `url.parse` warning on every request.

Live deployment (Hobby): <https://ufms-registry-server.vercel.app>

A push to `main` builds a production deployment. If the production aliases keep
serving the previous build, promote it by hand:

```bash
vercel promote <deployment-url>        # or Dashboard → Deployments → Promote to Production
```

In the Vercel project, create a **public** Blob store (Storage → Blob) and connect
it to the project. Then set:

```bash
vercel env add REGISTRY_API_KEY production        # optional bootstrap key
vercel env add REGISTRY_ADMIN_PASSWORD production
vercel env add REGISTRY_ADMIN_SECRET production   # optional, defaults to the password
```

Connecting the store is enough for the SDK (OIDC). Add `BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN`
only if you run the code outside Vercel or prefer a static token.

Vercel Authentication (SSO protection) must be **off** for the project, or every
`/mcp` call is redirected to a Vercel login page.

The first key is created at `/`; until then `/health` returns `503`
`unconfigured` and `/mcp` rejects requests. Blob reads are versioned by ETag, so a
new or revoked key is live within a few seconds (not instantly).


# Architecture How the repository is put together: what is authored, what is generated, how a session flows through it, and the invariants that keep the pieces in sync. - **Audience:** contributors and anyone debugging install or generation drift. - **Companion docs:** [Development](DEVELOPMENT.md) · [Skills](SKILLS.md) · [Catalog](../CATALOG.md) --- ## 1. System at a glance ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph Author["Authored (source of truth)"] A1["skills/<name>/"] A2["agents/*.md"] A3["commands/**/*.md"] end subgraph Generated["Generated (never hand-edited)"] G1[".opencode/skills/<name>/SKILL.md"] G2[".opencode/agents/*.md"] G3[".opencode/commands/**/*.md"] G4["CATALOG.md"] end subgraph Runtime["Runtime state"] R1[".ufme/ (per project)"] R2["~/.config/ufme/ (shared)"] end subgraph Install["Installed (user scope)"] I1["~/.config/opencode/agents/"] I2["~/.config/opencode/skills/"] I3["~/.config/opencode/commands/"] I4["~/.config/opencode/opencode.json"] end A1 --> G1 A2 --> G2 A3 --> G3 A1 --> G4 A2 --> G4 A3 --> G4 Author --> Install Author --> R1 Author --> R2 ``` Three things are **authored**: skills, agents, and commands. Everything under `.opencode/` and `CATALOG.md` is **generated**. Anything in `.ufme/` is **runtime state** produced by a session. --- ## 2. Source of truth and generated mirrors | Thing | Author here | Generated here | Regenerate with | |-------|-------------|----------------|-----------------| | Skills | `skills//` | `.opencode/skills//SKILL.md` | `python3 scripts/catalog.py` | | Agents | `agents/*.md` (flat, final names) | `.opencode/agents/*.md` | `python3 scripts/build-agents.py` | | Commands | `commands/**/*.md` | `.opencode/commands/**/*.md` | `python3 scripts/catalog.py` | | Catalog | — | `CATALOG.md` | `python3 scripts/catalog.py` | Both generators support `--check`, which exits non-zero on drift. CI runs both, so a hand-edited mirror or a stale catalog fails the build instead of shipping. ```mermaid flowchart LR E["Edit skills/ agents/ commands/"] --> G["Run generators"] G --> C{"--check passes?"} C -- no --> F["Fix source or rerun generator"] F --> G C -- yes --> P["Commit + push"] ``` --- ## 3. API_MAP · ARCHITECTURE · ..."] P --> E[".ufme/evidence/*.json"] S["~/.config/ufme/"] --> L["LIBRARY_REGISTRY.md + evidence"] L -->|search-libraries.py| P ``` | Location | Scope | Lifetime | Contents | |----------|-------|----------|----------| | `.ufme/` | One project | Committed by the user | Decisions, task state, design system, evidence JSON | | `.ufme/evidence/` | One project | Regenerated per run | `a11y-results.json`, `perf-results.json`, `visual-diff.json`, `quality-report.json` | | `~/.config/ufme/` | Whole machine | Survives reinstalls | Shared library registry, cross-project evidence | Seeding never overwrites an existing file, so project memory survives reinstall. --- ## 8. Execution pipeline The main skill runs the same seven phases in every profile; profiles change who does the work, not the order. ```mermaid flowchart LR A["01 Intake"] --> B["02 Research"] B --> C["03 Backend"] C --> D["04 Product"] D --> E["05 Prototype"] E --> F["06 Implement"] F --> G["07 Integrate"] G --> H{"Quality gate"} H -- findings --> F H -- pass --> I["Deliver"] ``` | Profile | Delegation | Use for | |---------|-----------|---------| | `lite` | Primary + builder | Small edits, quick prototypes | | `standard` | Balanced, includes backend + audit | Typical projects | | `advanced` | All roles, full audits | Complex projects | | `autonomous` | All roles, exhaustive verification | Unattended runs | --- ## 9. Evidence and the quality gate Audits do not report from screenshots or intuition; they read script output. ```mermaid flowchart TB B["browser-test.sh"] --> J1["browser-results.json"] A["audit-a11y.js"] --> J2["a11y-results.json"] P["audit-perf.sh"] --> J3["perf-results.json"] V["visual-diff.js"] --> J4["visual-diff.json"] S["detect-slop.py"] --> J5["slop-results.json"] J1 & J2 & J3 & J4 & J5 --> Q["quality-check.py"] Q --> R["quality-report.json"] R --> D{"PASS / FAIL / SKIPPED / BLOCKED"} ``` | Status | Meaning | |--------|---------| | `PASS` | Check ran, evidence is fresh and within threshold | | `FAIL` | Check ran and exceeded a threshold, or evidence was missing/stale | | `SKIPPED` | Preconditions missing (no browser, no URL); never counts as a pass | | `BLOCKED` | Required check could not run (for example, no visual baseline) | A required check that is skipped or has stale evidence **blocks** the gate. The design linter (`detect-slop.py`) is deliberately strict: fix the design, never the linter. --- ## 10. Registry (optional) `registry-server/` is a separate deployable: a Vercel function set that speaks MCP over JSON-RPC and stores one shared library registry. It is optional — the local Markdown registry is the default — and it fails closed: no configured key means `503`, a wrong key means `401`. See [registry-server/README.md](../registry-server/README.md) for endpoints, storage, and deployment. --- ## 11. Invariants These are the rules that keep the repository working. A change that breaks one of them is a bug, not a style choice. - [ ] `.opencode/` and `CATALOG.md` are never edited by hand. - [ ] An agent's frontmatter `name` equals its file stem. - [ ] Skills stay self-contained; an installed skill never reaches back into the repo. - [ ] Scripts resolve the repo root from their own path, never from `$PWD`. - [ ] Runtime state goes to `.ufme/`, never into the source tree. - [ ] The registry fails closed. - [ ] `detect-slop.py` is not weakened to make a site pass.

```bash

  --only a11y,perf --require a11y,perf \
```

## 9. Contracts worth knowing

**Root resolution.** Scripts find the repository root from their own location,
never from `$PWD`, so they work from any working directory:

| Language | Expression |
|----------|------------|
| Python (skill script) | `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]` (script → skill → skills → repo) |
| Python (repo script) | `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]` |
| Node | `path.resolve(__dirname, '..', '..', '..')` |

**Evidence freshness.** The quality gate compares the evidence file's mtime with
the run start. A gate that reuses yesterday's JSON reports `FAIL` — that is the
intended behaviour.

**Design gate.** `detect-slop.py` flags templated layouts, uniform entrance
motion, generic gradients, and an empty design system. Fix the design; do not
relax the detector.

## Overview

The `init-frontend` skill transforms a project brief into a complete, accessible, performant frontend project with a design system foundation. Unlike basic scaffolding tools that generate generic boilerplate, `init-frontend`:

- **Researches reference sites** — uses `ask-matt` to analyze URLs you provide before making design decisions
- **Enforces constraints** — anti-AI-slop rules prevent generic, low-quality output
- **Builds a design system** — Style Dictionary tokens, semantic color/typography/spacing scales
- **Bakes in accessibility** — WCAG 2.2 AA from day one, verified with static a11y gate
- **Enforces performance budgets** — LCP, INP, CLS, input size limits in CI
- **Supports templates** — 13 categories: landing, portfolio, blog, ecommerce, dashboard, admin, saas, docs, restaurant, realestate, event, nonprofit, resume

**No code is written until every design question is answered.** The scaffold script (`init-frontend.sh`) checks for `.ufme/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` and refuses to run if design questions haven't been answered.

```
     ↑                                                      │
```

## Design System & Anti-AI-Slop Rules

All init-frontend output enforces these constraints:

| Rule | What it means |
|------|---------------|
| **No Inter by default** | Choose typeface appropriate to project type |
| **No purple/blue gradients** | Avoid generic gradient backgrounds |
| **No hero+3-cards boilerplate** | No overused "hero section + three feature cards" layout |
| **No glassmorphism** | No frosted-glass backdrop-filter effects |
| **No sub-24px touch targets** | All interactive elements ≥ 24px × 24px |
| **No removed focus outlines** | `focus-visible` rings always preserved |
| **Words first** | Content hierarchy before decoration |
| **Constraints before options** | Encode limits, don't offer endless choice |

These rules are baked into the generated CSS and cannot be opted out of.

## Accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA)

| Requirement | Implementation |
|-------------|----------------|
| Semantic HTML | `<header>`, `<nav>`, `<main>`, `<footer>`, `<section>`, `<article>` |
| Focus visible rings | `outline: 2px solid var(--color-focus-ring)` on `:focus-visible` |
| Real labels | Every `<input>`, `<select>`, `<textarea>` has associated `<label>` |
| Text contrast | ≥ 4.5:1 for normal text, ≥ 3:1 for UI components |
| Keyboard nav | All interactive elements reachable via Tab |
| Reduced motion | `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` disables animations |
| Skip link | `.skip-link` for keyboard users to bypass navigation |
| Touch targets | Minimum 24px × 24px for all interactive elements |

Verified with **static a11y gate** via `scripts/a11y.cjs` — dependency-free, no Chrome needed.

# System Architecture

## Overview

ufmw-frontend-design is an OpenCode skill built on a multi-agent, multi-phase pipeline.
Agents collaborate through shared persistent project memory in `.ufme/` and a structured
delegation protocol. The system is platform-agnostic: it runs anywhere OpenCode, Node.js, Python, and a native Chromium or Firefox are available. Arch Linux specifics live in `core/ARCH_LINUX.md`.

## Layers

1. Entry layer — `ufmw-frontend-design` (the only `mode: primary`). Classifies the
   project, applies the execution profile, and delegates per `allowedAgents`.
2. Orchestration layer — `ufmw-orchestrator` (mode: subagent). Packs task context, enforces
   profile limits, owns `.ufme/AGENT_STATE.md` and `.ufme/TASKS.md`, resolves conflicts, and
   enforces acceptance criteria.
3. Specialist layer — `ufmw-designer`, `ufmw-builder`, `ufmw-backend-analyst`, and
   `ufmw-auditor` (mode: subagent). Each owns a domain and returns a structured result
   (status, files, decisions, open questions, blocking deps, next agent).
4. Reference-driven design layer — Selenium-based reference inspection (`reference-inspect.js`),
   element analysis (`reference-analyze.py`), matching (`reference-match.py`), adaptation
   (`reference-adapt.py`), and verification (`reference-verify.js`).
5. Execution layer — shell scripts in `skills/ufmw-frontend-design/scripts/` and the
   Selenium browser abstraction.
6. Memory layer — `.ufme/` templates and evidence. Every agent reads and updates the artifacts
   it owns.

## Data Flow

Brief/repo/screenshot/API docs/reference URL → intake → research → backend intelligence →
product intelligence → design → reference analysis → architecture → implementation → integration
→ browser execution → visual/accessibility/performance/security audits → fix & retest →
continuous improvement → delivery.

## Browser Stack

Native Selenium WebDriver with JavaScript bindings. Selenium Manager resolves and caches
matching Chromium and Firefox drivers automatically. Tests run headlessly by default.
Screenshots captured at mobile/tablet/laptop/desktop viewports, dark and light themes.

## Safety Boundaries

No sudo/pacman/systemctl/doas/pkexec/su. No Docker/Podman/containers. No Playwright.
Project-local npm dependencies only. Missing system browsers/libraries are reported to the
user with the exact setup command; browser testing is marked BLOCKED until confirmed installed.

## Reference-Driven Design Pipeline

1. User provides reference URL(s)
2. `reference-inspect.js` loads page in Selenium, extracts DOM + computed styles per element
3. `reference-analyze.py` groups elements by type, generates REFERENCES.md and ELEMENT_MAP.md
4. User specifies destination and aspects for each element
5. `reference-match.py` creates match plan
6. `reference-adapt.py` generates adapted component code (HTML/CSS with CSS variables)
7. `ufmw-builder` implements adapted elements in source code
8. `reference-verify.js` captures before/after screenshots, verifies implementation
9. `ufmw-auditor` includes reference-implementation findings in AUDIT_REPORT.md

# Reference-Driven Design Workflow

## Workflows

### 01 — Reference Discovery

## Goal
Classify the project, detect the existing stack, and identify reference URLs for design inspiration.

## Steps
1. **Ask the user:** "Do you have any reference website URLs you'd like to use as design inspiration?"
   - If **yes**: Ask for the link(s). Record each URL in `.ufme/REFERENCES.md`.
   - If **no**: Skip reference analysis; proceed with standard frontend engineering workflow.
2. Read `.ufme/AGENT_STATE.md` and `.ufme/ENVIRONMENT.md`.
3. Run `scripts/detect-stack.sh` to detect frontend and backend frameworks/tools.
4. Run `scripts/detect-platform.sh` to record host OS/compatibility (Arch Linux required).
5. Create `.ufme/PROJECT_SPEC.md` from the brief, repo, screenshot, or reference site.
6. Record classification: new, frontend-only, backend-only, or full-stack.
7. Update `.ufme/TASKS.md` (T-01) and `.ufme/AGENT_STATE.md`.
8. Delegate next: reference analysis (if references exist) or backend intelligence.

## Output
- `.ufme/PROJECT_SPEC.md`
- `.ufme/REFERENCES.md` (only if user provided reference URLs)
- `.ufme/TASKS.md` (T-01 marked COMPLETE)

### 02 — Reference Analysis

## Goal
Analyze reference websites, identify individual UI elements, extract DOM structure and
computed styles.

## Steps
1. Read `.ufme/PROJECT_SPEC.md` and `.ufme/REFERENCES.md`.
2. For each reference URL, run `scripts/reference-inspect.js <url>` to load in Selenium

# Agent Rules

## General rules (all agents)

1. Read `.ufme/AGENT_STATE.md` and `.ufme/ENVIRONMENT.md` before acting.
2. Update only the artifacts you own; do not overwrite another agent's output.
3. Return a structured result: status, files, decisions, open questions, blocking deps, next agent.
4. Never invent backend endpoints, fields, roles, permissions, or responses.
5. Never silently bypass missing system dependencies — record in `.ufme/ENVIRONMENT.md` and
   prompt the user with the exact setup command.
6. Use only free and open-source dependencies. Record UI libraries, icon sets, fonts, images,
   animation libraries, and templates in `.ufme/DECISIONS.md` before adding.
7. No sudo, pacman, systemctl, doas, pkexec, su. No Docker/Podman/containers. No Playwright.
8. Browser tests run headlessly by default; capture screenshots at all viewports.

## Specialist prohibitions

- ufme-backend-analyst: do not generate API code; produce evidence-based maps only.
- ufme-builder: do not invent backend capabilities; implement only what is confirmed.
- ufme-auditor: review actual Selenium screenshots, not mockups; consume script JSON evidence before screenshots.
- ufme-auditor: do not store or log secrets; flag exposed secrets instead.

## Escalation

Escalate to the orchestrator when: a dependency is missing, two agents conflict, a backend
capability cannot be confirmed, browser testing is blocked, or acceptance criteria cannot be
met without user action.

# Arch Linux Support

## Browser targets

- Native system Chromium and Firefox are the Selenium WebDriver targets.
- Selenium Manager (bundled with the `selenium-webdriver` npm package) resolves, downloads,
  and caches matching browser drivers automatically. Do not download drivers manually unless
  Selenium Manager fails.

## What this skill does NOT do on Arch Linux

- No `sudo`, `pacman`, `systemctl`, `doas`, `pkexec`, or `su`.
- No Docker, Podman, or containers.
- No Playwright and no `playwright install-deps`.
- No WebKit requirement.

## Missing browser dependencies

If Chromium or Firefox headless launch fails (e.g. missing `libnss3.so`, `libatk`,
`libcups`, `libdrm`, `libgbm`):

1. Stop the browser-testing step.
2. Record the missing dependency in `.ufme/ENVIRONMENT.md`.
3. Prompt the user with the exact command (e.g. `sudo pacman -S nss`).
4. Wait for the user to confirm installation before retrying.

## Supported platform

Arch Linux is the only supported platform. The scripts, agents, and Selenium
abstraction require Arch Linux with Node.js `^22.23.4 || ^24.22.1 || >=26.12.1`,
npm, system Chromium and Firefox, and the project-local audit dependencies.

# Multi-Agent Orchestration

## Collaboration model

1. Orchestrator reads `.ufme/AGENT_STATE.md`.
2. Orchestrator creates or updates `.ufme/TASKS.md`.
3. Orchestrator delegates one coherent task at a time to a specialist subagent.
4. Specialist returns a structured result:
   - Status: `COMPLETE`, `BLOCKED`, or `NEEDS_INPUT`
   - Files created or updated
   - Decisions made
   - Open questions
   - Blocking dependencies
   - Recommended next agent
5. Orchestrator updates `.ufme/AGENT_STATE.md` and `.ufme/TASKS.md`.
6. Orchestrator delegates the next dependent task.
7. Parallel work is allowed only when tasks do not modify the same files.
8. If two agents disagree, the orchestrator resolves the conflict and records the decision in
   `.ufme/DECISIONS.md`.

## Delegation examples

## Overview

universal-frontend-master is an OpenCode skill built on a multi-agent, multi-phase pipeline.
Agents collaborate through shared persistent project memory in `.ufme/` and a structured
delegation protocol. The system is platform-agnostic: it runs anywhere OpenCode, Node.js, Python, and a native Chromium or Firefox are available. Arch Linux specifics live in `core/ARCH_LINUX.md`.

## Quality gate semantics
- Required checks (`--require`, or the `audit` preset) cannot PASS when SKIPPED.
  A skipped required check makes the overall status BLOCKED.
- A check that exits 0 without fresh, structurally valid evidence is FAIL.
- Overall precedence: FAIL > BLOCKED > PASS.
- Visual regression treats a missing current screenshot as a failure and reports
  first-run baseline creation as BLOCKED, not PASS.
- `UFME_CHROME_FLAGS` overrides Lighthouse's Chrome flags (default
  `--headless=new`); container/CI runners usually need
  `--headless=new --no-sandbox --disable-dev-shm-usage`.

## Browser launch fails

Run `scripts/check-native-browser.sh`. If it reports a missing browser:
- Chromium missing: `sudo pacman -S chromium` (run yourself)
- Firefox missing: `sudo pacman -S firefox` (run yourself)

Browser testing stays BLOCKED until the dependency is confirmed installed. Non-browser work
continues.

The quality gate reports SKIPPED/BLOCKED when a dependency is missing. Install the full
project-local set:
```
npm install -D selenium-webdriver @axe-core/webdriverjs lighthouse pngjs pixelmatch
```
`install.sh` does this automatically when the target has a `package.json`.

## Selenium Manager cannot resolve a driver
Record the diagnostic in `.ufme/ENVIRONMENT.md` and prompt the user with a safe remediation
command. Do not download drivers manually unless Selenium Manager fails.

## No dev server responding
Start the local dev server (e.g. `npm run dev`) before running `browser-test.sh`.

## Permission denials
This agent never runs sudo/pacman/systemctl/doas/pkexec/su. Any system-level change requires
you to run it yourself. git push and npm publish require/deny per `opencode.json`.

- `.ufme/TASKS.md` (T-01 marked COMPLETE)
- `.ufme/AGENT_STATE.md` updated

# 02 — Research

## Goal
Research requirements, references, design inspiration, components, templates, fonts, icons,
images, and videos. Verify licenses and commercial-use permissions.

## Steps
1. Read `.ufme/PROJECT_SPEC.md` and any reference website/screenshot.
2. **Ask the user design-direction questions** (record answers in `.ufme/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md`):
   - What is the primary visual tone? (minimal, bold, playful, corporate, elegant, retro, futuristic)
   - Which motion graphics style? (none/subtle, entrance reveals, hover transitions, page-scroll animations, micro-interactions)
   - What animation palette? (soft/ease, bouncy/spring, sharp/linear, custom cubic-bezier, physics-based)
   - Preferred color palette? (brand colors, monochrome, gradient, pastel, neon, dark-first)
   - Typography direction? (serif, sans-serif, display, mono, custom brand font)
   - Are there brand assets to reference? (logo, existing website, brand guidelines)
3. Render the theme showcase so the user can see the palettes side by side:
   `scripts/theme-showcase.py --target .` → `.ufme/theme-showcase.pdf` (their current
   choice is marked and shown first).
4. Identify needed assets (fonts, icons, images, templates, components).
5. For each asset, verify license and commercial-use status.
6. Record asset decisions (name, repo/site, license, commercial-use, install method, reason)
   in `.ufme/DECISIONS.md` via the orchestrator.
7. Update `.ufme/TASKS.md` (T-03) and `.ufme/AGENT_STATE.md`.
8. Delegate next: backend intelligence (if backend) or product intelligence.

## Output
- Research notes
- Asset decisions in `.ufme/DECISIONS.md`
- Design-direction answers in `.ufme/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` (motion, animation, color, typography, brand assets)
- `.ufme/theme-showcase.pdf` — every curated theme rendered for review
- `.ufme/TASKS.md` (T-03 COMPLETE)

# 03 — Backend Intelligence

## Goal
Analyze the backend/API and produce evidence-based API, auth, authorization, error, and
capability maps. Never invent endpoints, fields, roles, permissions, or responses.

## Steps
1. Read backend repo and API docs (OpenAPI, Swagger, Postman, AsyncAPI).
2. Run `scripts/backend-discovery.sh` to detect the backend framework.
3. Run `scripts/enhance-backend-discovery.py` to parse OpenAPI/Swagger/Postman/GraphQL/
   AsyncAPI contracts and extract operations, schemas, auth, errors; results go to
   `.ufme/BACKEND_CONTRACTS.md` classified CONFIRMED / INFERRED / UNKNOWN /
   NOT_FOUND / NOT_APPLICABLE.
4. Create `.ufme/API_MAP.md` with columns:
   Method | Path | Purpose | Auth | Request | Response | Errors | Frontend use | Evidence
   (only from CONFIRMED capabilities).
5. Create `.ufme/BACKEND_CAPABILITIES.md`, classifying each item:
   CONFIRMED / INFERRED / MISSING_BACKEND / NOT_APPLICABLE / DO_NOT_BUILD.
6. Create `.ufme/AUTHENTICATION_MAP.md` (flows, roles, permissions, token storage).
7. Create `.ufme/ERROR_HANDLING.md` (error codes, frontend mapping, user-facing messages).
8. Update `.ufme/TASKS.md` (T-04) and `.ufme/AGENT_STATE.md`.
9. Delegate next: product intelligence.

## Output
- `.ufme/API_MAP.md`
- `.ufme/BACKEND_CAPABILITIES.md`
- `.ufme/AUTHENTICATION_MAP.md`
- `.ufme/ERROR_HANDLING.md`

# 04 — Product Intelligence

## Goal
Create PRD, sitemap, user flows, feature matrix, user roles, and acceptance criteria. Map
every confirmed backend capability to a frontend feature or document why it is absent.

## Steps
1. Read `.ufme/PROJECT_SPEC.md`, `.ufme/API_MAP.md`, `.ufme/BACKEND_CAPABILITIES.md`.
2. Create `.ufme/PRD.md` (goals, user roles, acceptance criteria).
3. Create `.ufme/SITEMAP.md` (page hierarchy and routes).
4. Create `.ufme/USER_FLOWS.md` (key user journeys).
5. Create `.ufme/FEATURES.md` (feature matrix mapped to confirmed backend capabilities;
   document why any capability is absent).
6. Update `.ufme/TASKS.md` (T-05) and `.ufme/AGENT_STATE.md`.
7. Delegate next: design.

## Output
- `.ufme/PRD.md`
- `.ufme/SITEMAP.md`
- `.ufme/USER_FLOWS.md`
- `.ufme/FEATURES.md`

# 05 — Prototype

## Goal
Create the design system, wireframes, and component architecture from the PRD and API map.

## Steps
1. Read `.ufme/PRD.md`, `.ufme/API_MAP.md`, `.ufme/SITEMAP.md`, `.ufme/USER_FLOWS.md`,
   `.ufme/FEATURES.md`, and `.ufme/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` (motion/animation/color/typography answers).
2. Create `.ufme/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` (canonical path only — no `.ufme/design/` copy).
   Start with `## Design direction`: tone, two distinct type roles with real typefaces,
   palette rationale, layout concept, and motion hierarchy (at least two treatments).
   Then tokens (typography, spacing, color; component architecture; responsive rules;
   animation guidance; accessible UI patterns). Do not start implementation while
   `detect-slop.py --path <src> --design .ufme/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` still reports
   `design-system-incomplete`.
   - Include motion graphics specification: entrance reveals, hover states, scroll animations,
     micro-interactions with easing curves and duration. Vary them by hierarchy.
   - Include animation palette: preferred easing (ease, ease-in, ease-out, ease-in-out, custom),
     duration ranges (fast 150-300ms, normal 300-500ms, slow 500-800ms), stagger delays.
3. Run `scripts/generate-prototype.py` to produce HTML/CSS prototype pages from the
   sitemap routes and design tokens; output isolated in `prototypes/`.
4. Produce wireframes (low-fidelity page layouts).
5. Record any new asset (font, icon, image) in `.ufme/DECISIONS.md`.
6. Run `scripts/discover-assets.py` to inventory project images/fonts/videos with license
   hints into `.ufme/ASSET_MANIFEST.md`.
7. Update `.ufme/TASKS.md` (T-06) and `.ufme/AGENT_STATE.md`.
8. Delegate next: frontend architecture.

## Output
- `.ufme/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` (including motion graphics and animation palette)
- Wireframes
- Component architecture

# 06 — Implementation

## Goal
Build pages, reusable components, navigation, forms, state, loading/error/empty states,
responsive layouts, animations, and PWA readiness where justified.

## Steps
1. Read `.ufme/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `.ufme/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md`, `.ufme/TASKS.md` (approved
   feature slice).
2. Implement the next approved feature slice preserving existing architecture.
3. Include loading, error, and empty states on every data-dependent view.
4. Implement responsive layouts at mobile/tablet/laptop/desktop breakpoints.
5. Implement the motion hierarchy from `.ufme/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` — not one shared entrance
   variant on every section. No control without behaviour; no permanent scrim hiding the
   primary work; verify the declared grid actually lays out.
6. Update `.ufme/TASKS.md` via the orchestrator.
7. Delegate next: integration (if backend) or browser execution.

## Output
- Frontend source files (pages, components, layouts, forms)
- `.ufme/TASKS.md` updated

# 07 — Integration

## Goal
Connect the frontend to confirmed backend endpoints.

## Steps
1. Read `.ufme/API_MAP.md`, `.ufme/AUTHENTICATION_MAP.md`, `.ufme/ERROR_HANDLING.md`,
   `.ufme/BACKEND_CAPABILITIES.md`.
2. Implement typed API client using only confirmed endpoints.
3. Implement authentication flows, authorization-aware UI, validation, error handling,
   retries where appropriate, network failure states.
4. Do not call endpoints absent from `.ufme/API_MAP.md`.
5. Update `.ufme/TASKS.md` via the orchestrator.
6. Delegate next: browser execution.

## Output
- Typed API client
- Auth flows, authorization-aware UI, validation, error handling, retries, network failure states

# 08 — Browser Execution

## Goal
Run native Selenium WebDriver browser tests (Chromium preferred, Firefox fallback) against
the local dev server; capture screenshots and failures.

## Steps
1. Run `scripts/check-native-browser.sh` (detect Chromium/Firefox, Selenium Manager,
   minimal headless launch).
2. If browser launch fails: save error to `.ufme/evidence/browser-setup-error.txt`, prompt
   user with exact setup command, mark browser testing BLOCKED, continue non-browser work.
3. Start the local dev server.
4. Run `scripts/browser-test.sh <URL>` (default `http://localhost:5173`).
5. Capture screenshots into `.ufme/evidence/screenshots/` at mobile/tablet/laptop/desktop,
   dark + light themes.
6. Collect console errors, failed requests, broken links, interaction failures.
7. Save `.ufme/evidence/browser-results.json`.
8. Update `.ufme/TASKS.md` (T-10/T-11) and `.ufme/AGENT_STATE.md`.
9. Delegate next: visual audit.

## Output
- `.ufme/evidence/screenshots/*.png`
- `.ufme/evidence/browser-results.json`
- `.ufme/evidence/browser-setup-error.txt` (on failure)

# 09 — Visual Audit

## Goal
Review actual Selenium screenshots; produce severity-ranked visual audit; verify fixes.

## Steps
1. Read screenshots in `.ufme/evidence/screenshots/`.
2. Create `.ufme/VISUAL_AUDIT.md` with table:
   ID | Page | Viewport | Screenshot | Severity | Issue | Likely cause | Suggested fix | Owner | Status | Retest evidence
3. Rank issues: critical / major / minor.
4. Review every viewport against: hierarchy (one clear focal point), grid integrity
   (declared columns appear), media legibility (primary work visible without hover),
   dead controls (click every button/link), motion variety, overflow, contrast.
   An empty table is FAIL, not PASS.
5. For critical/major issues, return to builder (via orchestrator) for fixes.
6. After fixes, capture fresh screenshots and update Status/Retest evidence.
7. Update `.ufme/TASKS.md` (T-13) and `.ufme/AGENT_STATE.md`.
8. Delegate next: accessibility audit.

## Output
- `.ufme/VISUAL_AUDIT.md`
- Fresh verification screenshots (on fix)

# 10 — Accessibility Audit

## Goal
Check semantic HTML, landmarks, headings, labels, focus visibility, keyboard operation,
contrast, touch targets, reduced motion, screen-reader semantics. Target WCAG 2.1 AA.

## Steps
1. Read frontend source and `.ufme/VISUAL_AUDIT.md`.
2. Run axe-core accessibility checks where a browser is available.
3. Record findings (semantic HTML, landmarks, headings, labels, focus, keyboard, contrast,
   touch targets, reduced motion, screen-reader semantics).
4. Return critical/major a11y findings to builder via orchestrator.
5. Update `.ufme/TASKS.md` (T-14) and `.ufme/AGENT_STATE.md`.
6. Delegate next: performance audit.

## Output
- Accessibility findings (WCAG 2.1 AA)
- `.ufme/TASKS.md` updated

# 11 — Performance Audit

## Goal
Measure Core Web Vitals-oriented lab metrics, bundle size, image optimization, caching,
network requests, and Lighthouse results.

## Steps
1. Build production bundle.
2. Serve production build locally.
3. Measure bundle size, image optimization, caching, network requests.
4. Run Lighthouse audit against the locally served production build when possible.
5. Record lab metrics and recommendations.
6. Return critical performance findings to builder via orchestrator.
7. Update `.ufme/TASKS.md` (T-15) and `.ufme/AGENT_STATE.md`.
8. Delegate next: security audit.

## Output
- Performance findings (lab metrics, bundle size, images, caching, network, Lighthouse)

# 12 — Security Audit

## Goal
Check XSS, unsafe HTML rendering, CSRF, CORS, CSP, cookies, token storage, exposed secrets,
dependency vulnerabilities, and unsafe client-side authorization assumptions.

## Steps
1. Read frontend source, `.ufme/API_MAP.md`, `.ufme/AUTHENTICATION_MAP.md`, package.json.
2. Run dependency audit (npm audit) where supported.
3. Check XSS, unsafe HTML rendering, CSRF, CORS, CSP, cookies, token storage, exposed
   secrets, client-side authorization assumptions.
4. Never store or log secrets; flag exposed secrets instead.
5. Return critical security findings immediately to the orchestrator.
6. Update `.ufme/TASKS.md` (T-16) and `.ufme/AGENT_STATE.md`.
7. Delegate next: continuous improvement / fix & retest.

## Output
- Security findings

# 13 — Continuous Improvement

## Goal
Fix critical and major findings, retest, repeat until acceptance criteria pass or
limitations are documented.

## Steps
1. Aggregate findings from VISUAL_AUDIT.md, accessibility, performance, security audits into
   `.ufme/AUDIT_REPORT.md`.
2. Prioritize critical and major findings.
3. Return fixes to builder (implementation and integration) via orchestrator; retest after each fix.
4. Record conflict resolutions and dependency decisions in `.ufme/DECISIONS.md`.
5. Update `.ufme/AGENT_STATE.md` and `.ufme/TASKS.md`.
6. **Self-improvement**: run `scripts/self-improve.py` to audit the skill itself
   (templates, agents, scripts, docs, OpenCode install). Apply fixes to
   `skills/universal-frontend-master/` and re-deploy changed agents/skill files.
7. Repeat until acceptance criteria pass or limitations explicitly documented.
8. Delegate next: delivery.

## Output
- `.ufme/AUDIT_REPORT.md`
- `.ufme/DECISIONS.md` updated
- `.ufme/TASKS.md` updated
- `.ufme/SELF_IMPROVEMENT.md` (skill self-audit)

Hand off the complete, tested, production-ready website.

- `.ufme/SKILL_VALIDATION.md`
